name: English Electric (BAC) Canberra T.17, 360 Squadron

published.source: en.wikipedia 'English Electric Canberra', B.2: length 65 ft 6 in (19.96 m), span 64 ft 0 in (19.51 m, without tip tanks), height 15 ft 8 in (4.78 m). No T.17 length is published in the sources fetched: 21.66 m is MEASURED (CC: radome tip to nacelle lip 6.65 m against the B.2's 4.95 m, i.e. the B.2 plus 1.70 m), so the length rule checks the model against its own measurement, not a published figure

engine.row: js/eras.js gbr_e60_ewair: cat aircraft, layer air, jet, jam 6; js/aar_specs.js: null (no tanker gear, no probe)
engine.current_nodes: tools/model3d/dump.js on the tree before this change: one engine node, the group 'gear'.
engine.frame: Built in the drawing frame of the file (z 0 the fuselage axis, ground z -1.66) and stood level on its wheels by the kit's stance (pitch 0 about the main-wheel contact), so the dumped model stands on z 0: every z below is the as-stood height = drawing z + 1.66.
engine.shared_file: js/hero/gb_vforce.js also builds the Valiant (gbr_e50_tanker, and gbr_e50_heavybomber through js/hero/redo_bombers.js) and the Victor (gbr_e60_tanker): only the Canberra's builder changed; those three rows dump byte-identical before and after (dump json compared without buildMs).

references.name: [CA] Canberra B.2 3-view silhouette, side (aft of the nacelle lip)
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'English Electric Canberra B2 3-view silhouette.jpg', 927 x 1281
references.note: Nose left in the sheet: flipped. Scale on the side view's own length: B.2 nose col 49 to tail bullet col 892 = 843 px over the published 19.96 m = 42.23 px/m (the plan is drawn at 40.48 along / 41.98 across, so each view is scaled on its own). Second dimension: fuselage depth at col 357 rows 1186-1266 = 80 px = 1.89 m against CB's 78 in (1.98 m) - 4.5 per cent thin, the silhouette's outline width. The T.17 is the B.2 plus 1.70 m forward of the nacelle lip (CC), so only the part aft of the lip (x < 4.18) is compared: window_m. Origin: the tail tip (col 892) is model x -10.83; the fuselage axis (row 1226 at col 357) is z 0.02 in the drawing frame = 1.68 as stood. The T.17's tail-cone fairing (CC) differs from the B.2 bullet: ignore_m. Gear hidden (the drawing is gear-up).

references.name: [CA] Canberra B.2 3-view silhouette, plan
references.note: Nose up in the sheet: rotate 90. Along: rows 254-1062 = 808 px over 19.96 m = 40.48 px/m; across: cols 50-869 = 819 px over the 19.51 m span = 41.98 px/m - 3.6 per cent apart, so advisory only (the silhouette has no tip tanks; CB and every photograph has them, the model draws them). Tailplane span measured across: row 1020 cols 287-646 = 359 px = 8.55 m (41.98).

references.name: [CA] Canberra B.2 3-view silhouette, head-on
references.note: Span 817 px (cols 47-864) over 19.51 m = 41.9 px/m. The fuselage circle's foot is row 184; its centre taken 41 px above (1.98 m deep). Gear-up and without tip tanks, and the T.17's bigger nose stands in front: advisory. Used for the nacelle centres at y +-3.05 m and the dihedral (2 deg to the nacelle, 4.35 deg outboard, CB).

references.name: [CC] WH664 of 360 Sqn in flight, starboard side, gear down
references._landmarks: the stations measured on this photograph (intake lip, wheels, canopy) are distances along the level airframe, so their landmarks name ref 0 (level, unpitched side axes), not this pitched overlay
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'English Electric Canberra T17, UK - Air Force AN1155605.jpg', 1024 x 678
references.note: Square on, long lens. Scale 44.2 px/m from the B.2's 15.0 m from nacelle lip to tail tip (663 px); fuselage depth 87 px for 78 in = 43.9 agrees. Radome tip (987, 357) = model (10.83, -0.05 drawing = 1.61 as stood). Measured on it: nose to nacelle lip 294 px = 6.65 m; canopy 2.45-3.85 m aft of the tip, its top 0.15 m over the spine; cheek fairing front 0.77 m (col 953), aft point 2.19 m (col 890); keel fairing under the nose 0.8-4.1 m; HF mast on the spine at 7.67 m (col 648) with the wire to the fin top; the fin aerial fairing at about 2.45 m up the fin, cols 127-160; the tail-cone fairing 0.32 m across, cols 32-60. In flight the airframe is about 1.5 deg nose-up on the picture's horizontal (pitch_deg, turned about the radome tip; the best free fit: IoU 0.726 level, 0.767 at 1.0, 0.771 at 1.5, 0.730 at 2.0); it is also banked a little, which the side overlay cannot take out. Its roundels, fin flash, codes, serial and squadron badge are NOT drawn; the camouflage pattern is not drawn either (plain paint, AGENT_POLICY 6).

references.name: [CD] WH646 of 360 Sqn at Aviano 1989, starboard side on the ground
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Canberra T17 360 Sqn at Aviano AB 1989.JPEG', 960 x 636
references.note: For the reviewer: the level sit on the ground (belly 0.70 m clear at the nose wheel, 27 : 78 px), the twin nose wheels, the single mains, the cheek fairing, the tail-cone fairing and the probe behind it, the fin aerial fairing. Hazy and taken in flat light: the finish reads paler than it is.

references.name: [CE] WH863 nose section close up (Newark Air Museum)
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'EE Canberra T17 WH863 nose (6806456188).jpg', 960 x 640
references.note: For the reviewer: the black radome cap (front 0.72 m), a cheek fairing each side with its bulbous front, the small dark fairing on the nose top, the crew door and equipment panel outlines, the green upper paint over light grey under the nose. Its numbers and stencils are not drawn.

references.name: [CF] WH740 at East Midlands, starboard quarter
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'WH740 English Electric Canberra T17 ... 070924.jpg', 1600 x 521
references.note: For the reviewer: the tip tanks green over grey, split at their widest line; the nacelle intake with its starter bullet on vanes; the big outboard main-leg door; the HF mast and wire; the light grey undersides of wing and nacelle. The red intake ring is museum paint and the camouflage pattern is not drawn.

references.name: [CB] Martin B-57A 3-view line drawing (dimensioned)
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Martin B-57A Canberra 3-view line drawing.png'
references.note: Dimensions only (the licence-built B.2 airframe, in inches): tailplane span 336 in, 10 deg tailplane dihedral, wing dihedral 2 deg inboard and 4 deg 21 min outboard, track 189.375 in (4.81 m), wing root chord 228 in, fuselage depth 78 in, main tyre rolling radius 18.3 in, nose tyre 10.6 in, tip tanks 170.4 in long and 32 in across centred on the 767.42 in tip-to-tip line (y +-9.745 m).

must_show: the T.17's long ECM nose: radome tip at x 10.83 (d 0), the nose 6.65 m from tip to nacelle lip (B.2: 4.95), its black radome cap over the front 0.72 m (x 10.11 to 10.83), square-topped section 0.7 m half width

a cheek fairing each side of the nose at y +-0.79 m, z 1.59, 0.48 m deep (CC rows 350-372 at 44.2 px/m) and about 0.42 m wide: full, blunt front at d 0.77 (x 10.06), pointed aft end at d 2.2 (x 8.6), painted like the nose round it (CE shows no dark cap on it) (CC, CE)
the small dark fairing on the nose top at d 0.55-1.25 (x 10.28 to 9.58, CE) and the light keel fairing under the nose from d 0.85 to 4.1 (x 9.98 to 6.73, CC)
the fighter-type bubble canopy offset nothing - on the centre line from d 2.45 to 3.85 (x 8.38 to 6.98), its top 0.15 m over the spine (z 2.78), frames at d 2.68 and 3.55
round fuselage 1.98 m deep, deepest over the wing, tapering to a tail-cone fairing 0.32 m across from d 21.1 to 21.66 (x -10.27 to -10.83) with a dark cap (CC, CD)
straight wing: constant 5.78 m chord to the nacelles, tapered outboard, leading edge d 8.02, dihedral 2 deg to y 3.05 and 4.35 deg outboard (CA, CB)
Avon nacelles through the wing at y +-3.05 m: intake lip at d 6.65 (x 4.18) with the starter bullet on three vanes, the jet pipes out at d 14.36 (x -3.53) (CC, CF)

tip tanks 4.33 m long, 0.81 m across, centred at y +-9.745 m, from d 9.0 (x 1.83) to 13.33 (x -2.5), the jettison vent pipe aft of it to x -2.72, green over grey split at their widest line, each with a small vent fin aft (CB, CF)

the square-topped fin to z 4.74, its trailing edge at x -9.98 (z 4.0), -9.91 (z 4.4), -9.72 (z 4.7) and the top-rear corner rounded (CA side; CC about -9.8) with its curved dorsal fillet from d 16.8, the aerial fairing on each side at z 4.11 (fin height 2.45 m), and the low tailplane at z 2.41 root with 10 deg dihedral, span 8.54 m (CA, CB, CC)
the HF mast on the spine at d 7.67 (x 3.16) and its wire to the fin's leading edge at z 4.64 (CC, CF)
gear: twin nose wheels at d 4.7 (x 6.13), single main wheels at d 9.1 (x 1.73) on a 4.81 m track (y +-2.40), the big main-leg door outboard of each wheel (CC, CB, CF)

plain paint: grey-green above (shown about 0x737c69 at the game camera), light aircraft grey below (about 0xb3b7b0), split low on the fuselage side (24 per cent of the depth up from the belly) and on the wing at the leading edge; panel lines, hinge lines, the bomb-bay (ECM bay) doors d 7.0-13.2 on the sheet; team colour only in a small strip on each upper outer wing at y +-8.1

the demarcation height on the fuselage side (24 per cent of the depth from the belly, from CC and CF), and the exact grey-green: 360 Sqn T.17s wore dark green / dark sea grey camouflage over light aircraft grey (CC, CF) and a lighter late scheme (CD); the model takes one plain grey-green between the two upper colours, as the brief asks
